blocks.x: Beckham takes £39m dividend as World Cup deals drive record profits
David Beckham has taken a $51m (£39m) dividend from his business empire fuelled by a series of deals with brands for the Fifa World Cup.
Beckham appeared in about a dozen ad campaigns across this summer’s tournament in the US, working with brands including Lenovo, McDonald’s, Bank of America, Verizon and PepsiCo’s crisps brand Lay’s.
The World Cup work helped to fuel a record year for DRJB Holdings, the commercial company for Beckham’s brands business, where revenues surged by a fifth to $110.5m last year, from $92.3m in 2024.
Pre-tax profits also climbed to a record $65.7m, a 46% increase on 2024.

Havertz returns to Arsenal for treatment after suffering injnury on Germany duty
Kai Havertz will return to Arsenal for treatment after he sustained a “muscle sprain” while on Germany duty.
Havertz was forced off in the 30th minute of the nation’s 1-1 draw with the Netherlands due to a hamstring problem.
The German FA confirmed a subsequent scan had identified that the 27-year-old had suffered a sprain and he has now left Jurgen Klopp’s squad.

Havertz was sidelined for nearly five months with a knee injury last season, but he has started all five of Arsenal’s Premier League games so far, preferred to Viktor Gyokeres by manager Mikel Arteta.
The Premier League champions are hopeful Havertz’s latest setback is not serious.
Arsenal will next be in action when they host Leeds at the Emirates Stadium on 10 October. Press Association

blocks.x: Craig Bellamy said the Liverpool forward Lewis Koumas deserves to perform on the biggest stages after defeat to Portugal and promised to make changes for Sunday’s visit to Denmark.

Wales, who fly to Copenhagen on Saturday, lost their Nations League opener after Joao Felix scored the only goal in Lisbon. Koumas, who started the game on the left flank, spurned a golden chance to equalise late on but Bellamy was impressed by the 21-year-old. “I was looking at him and I thought he was outstanding,” Bellamy said. “I was thinking: he belongs here, he belongs here. There’s your headline.”

Koumas has also made a big impression on Andoni Iraola and his staff, featuring in five of Liverpool’s seven matches this season. When it was put to Bellamy that Koumas, who spent last season on loan at Birmingham and Hull, decided to stay at Liverpool this season to prove himself, Bellamy interrupted: “No, they kept him on at Anfield. You don’t get the choice to stay. If they want to keep you, they keep you. They thought he was too good, he ain’t going [anywhere].”

Bellamy acknowledged Wales expended a lot of energy in defeat at Jose Alvalade Stadium, where Cristiano Ronaldo won his 234th cap. “We are going to need to change players,” he said. “The turnaround is so quick, so demanding, we need to change players and we will do.

“They’re running machines [Portugal], that’s why they’re at this level. You don’t always pick up on the intensity – if you pay £140m for a player, you’re paying for his running level as well as his ability. A lot of these players are game-ready and they have a ridiculous intensity to match.”

“It’s a very good comparison,” James Garner says, and he is not kidding. It came from Thomas Tuchel in March after the England manager had watched the Everton midfielder impress on his international debut against Uruguay. He was up against Federico Valverde and Tuchel went big with his praise. Garner was a “mini Valverde”, he said after the 1-1 draw at Wembley.

It was surely too much, despite the prefix that Tuchel attached, yet it was possible to see where he was coming from. Like Valverde, Garner wants to operate in central midfield but he can play at right-back or on the wing. And like Valverde, who they called El Pajarito – or the Little Bird – when he was a kid, Garner can sometimes fly a bit under the radar.
The Spain manager Luis de la Fuente has sent an ominious message to the rest of world football: what they did at the World Cup isn’t enough to keep them winning. The coach said:

double quotation markThis team won’t stop; it wants more and more, to be the best. I will tell them that too. What we did at the World Cup is not enough to keep us winning games or to beat England. You have to be better. That’s our culture and our mentality, our attitude, so I have no doubts and no worries.

US men’s national team head coach Mauricio Pochettino says he regrets not being “more involved” in the situation surrounding US forward Folarin Balogun at this summer’s World Cup.

Balogun was given a red card after a challenge against Bosnia and Herzegovina defender Tarik Muharemović, which by rule is accompanied with a one-game suspension. Balogun’s ban for the next game against Belgium was suspended after the US Soccer Federation and US president Donald Trump lobbied Fifa, with Trump saying that he personally placed a call to Fifa president Gianni Infantino to ask the ruling be reviewed. Infantino maintains that the decision to reinstate Balogun was made independently by Fifa’s disciplinary committee.

The entire affair cast a pall over what had been an otherwise positive tournament for the US to that point. Belgium’s players and coaches said in the wake of it that it provided extra motivation ahead of the match. Balogun himself later spoke of having felt uncomfortable with the attention the situation placed upon him.

Wrexham have confirmed that Humphrey Ker is stepping down from the club’s board and as a trustee. Ker was a key part of Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac buying the club five years ago and has continued to play a role during their promotion successes.
Ker, who was a part of the Disney documentary about the club, said:
double quotation markWorking for and representing Wrexham AFC and the wider town has been the greatest honour of my life.
I am proud of the part I have played in the Club’s remarkable journey, both on and off the field.

Chelsea charged by FA over alleged discriminatory chanting against Fulham

Some breaking news for you, Chelsea have been charged with breaching a Football Association rule in their 3-2 win over Fulham last month. The governing body alleges the club broke rule E21 in the ninth minute of the match where the Blues “failed to ensure its spectators and/or supporters did not behave in an improper, offensive, abusive or insulting way. It’s further alleged that this behaviour was discriminatory in that it included a reference, whether express or implied, to religion or belief”.

Anthony Gordon has sided with Thomas Tuchel’s assertion that controlling games through possession is not part of English football’s DNA. Although Gordon revealed surprise at being substituted when England were 1-0 up in their World Cup semi-final against Argentina, the winger refused to blame the defeat on Tuchel’s decisions and argued that wider cultural issues influenced the side’s collapse.

England’s perennial struggle to keep the ball when under pressure flared when a place in the final was within touching distance in July, allowing Argentina to fight back and go through with two late goals. The pain has not gone away and there has been intense scrutiny of Tuchel’s role in Atlanta. The head coach’s tactical choices were criticised and he faced a backlash after saying “ball possession” was not in his team’s DNA.
